annotations.text:
OPTION A — EVEN RAIL

Equal gaps, each step smaller and softer.

Reads most clearly as "a line of things to come". Most literal to your frame note.

Tradeoff: the even spacing eats width fast — only about two and a half cards fit before the edge, so it undersells how much is left.

OPTION B — DECK

Heavy overlap; you see four slivers in the space one spaced card would take.

Biggest live card of the four, and it genuinely communicates "four more".

Tradeoff: slivers carry no information — you can tell there are more, not what they are.

OPTION C — PERSPECTIVE

Trailing cards turned away on a receding plane, cover-flow style.

The most physical read of "art gallery" — depth does the work, so less blur is needed.

Tradeoff: the most dated of the four, and 3D transforms plus blur are the combination most likely to stutter on older iPhones.

OPTION D — TWO THEN STACK

The next card stays readable with real room; the last three collapse into a sliver stack.

Only option that answers both "what's next" and "how much is left".

Tradeoff: two rhythms in one row — it can read as a mistake rather than a decision if the spacing isn't right.

The one thing worth getting right regardless of which option you pick: the demo starts looping as the card begins growing, not when it lands. Apple Tips does this — the motion never pauses. Starting the loop on arrival puts a dead beat right where the user is looking.
